title: Linkage disequilibrium as named allelic association
dek: Wikipedia LD: D, D', r² between loci. In Mtb it is often clonality in costume. Fine-mapping and GWAS peaks depend on it.
story: Linkage disequilibrium on Wikipedia is association between alleles at different loci, measured with D, D', r². In recombining sexual populations it traces haplotype history. In clonal Mtb it often traces lineage.
A GWAS peak is an LD neighbourhood. Reporting the smallest-p SNP as causal without that sentence is the decoder-ring error on stats-gwas.
r²=1 means you cannot statistically split the two sites in this sample. Functional follow-up is then obligatory if you care which nucleotide.
deep: D' =1 can still have r²<1 because of allele frequencies.
Population structure inflates LD measures if you mix lineages and call it one population (stats-population-structure).
Recombination breakpoints in mixed-ancestry NTM/Mtb mosaics make a single LD map a lie.
Do not 'correct LD' with Bonferroni as if m independent tests.

visual.caption: Two sites, an r² edge, a peak that cannot split them. Lineage can generate the same edge without a causal pair.
